```lua
local config = {}
local current_section = ""
local errors = {}

local function trim(s)
    return s:match("^%s*(.-)%s*$")
end

for line in io.lines() do
    line = trim(line)
    if line == "" or line:sub(1, 1) == ";" or line:sub(1, 1) == "#" then
        goto continue
    end

    if line:sub(1, 1) == "[" and line:sub(#line, -1) == "]" then
        current_section = trim(line:sub(2, -2))
    else
        local eq_idx = line:find("=")
        if not eq_idx or eq_idx == 1 then
            table.insert(errors, "Line without '=' or with empty key: " .. line)
        else
            local key = trim(line:sub(1, eq_idx - 1))
            local value = trim(line:sub(eq_idx + 1))
            if key == "" then
                table.insert(errors, "Empty key in: " .. line)
            else
                local full_key = current_section .. (current_section == "" and "" or ".") .. key
                config[full_key] = value
            end
        end
    end
    ::continue::
end

local sorted_keys = {}
for k in pairs(config) do table.insert(sorted_keys, k) end
table.sort(sorted_keys, function(a, b)
    local i, j = 1, 1
    while i <= #a and j <= #b and a:byte(i) == b:byte(j) do
        i = i + 1
        j = j + 1
    end
    return a:byte(i) < b:byte(j) or (a:byte(i) == b:byte(j) and #a < #b)
end

for _, k in ipairs(sorted_keys) do
    print(k .. "=" .. config[k])
end

if #errors > 0 then
    print("errors: " .. table.concat(errors, ", "))
end
```

local states = {}
local current_state = nil
local accumulated_dt = 0

local function switch(name, ...)
    if current_state and current_state.leave then current_state.leave(...) end
    current_state = states[name]
    if current_state and current_state.enter then current_state.enter(...) end
end

-- Game Data
local player = { x = 400, y = 500, speed = 300 }
local obstacles = {}
local score = 0
local startTime = 0

-- State: Menu
states.menu = {
    enter = function() print("Game Loaded") end,
    draw = function()
        love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
        love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1)
        love.graphics.printf("DODGE GAME\nPress SPACE to Start\nPress ESC to Quit", 0, 200, love.graphics.getWidth(), "center")
    end,
    keypressed = function(key)
        if key == "space" then switch("play") end
        if key == "escape" then love.event.quit() end
    end
}

-- State: Play
states.play = {
    enter = function()
        obstacles = {}
        score = 0
        startTime = love.timer.getTime()
    end,
    update = function(dt)
        accumulated_dt = accumulated_dt + dt
        -- Player Movement
        if love.keyboard.isDown("left") then player.x = player.x - player.speed * accumulated_dt end
        if love.keyboard.isDown("right") then player.x = player.x + player.speed * accumulated_dt end
        
        -- Obstacle Logic
        if math.random() < 0.05 then
            table.insert(obstacles, {x = math.random(0, love.graphics.getWidth()), y = -20})
        end
        
        for i = #obstacles, 1, -1 do
            local o = obstacles[i]
            o.y = o.y + 200 * accumulated_dt
            if o.y > love.graphics.getHeight() then table.remove(obstacles, i) else end
            
            -- Collision
            if math.abs(o.x - player.x) < 30 and math.abs(o.y - player.y) < 30 then
                switch("game_over")
            end
        end
        score = math.floor(love.timer.getTime() - startTime)
    end,
    draw = function()
        love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
        love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1)
        love.graphics.rectangle("fill", player.x - 15, player.y - 15, 30, 30)
        for _, o in ipairs(obstacles) do
            love.graphics.rectangle("fill", o.x, o.y, 30, 30)
        end
        love.graphics.print("Score: " .. score, 10, 10)
    end,
    keypressed = function(key)
        if key == "p" then switch("pause") end
    end
}

-- State: Pause
states.pause = {
    enter = function() end,
    update = function(dt) end, -- Don't update game logic
    draw = function()
        love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(0, 0, 0, 0.5)
        love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1)
        love.graphics.printf("PAUSED", 0, 200, love.graphics.getWidth(), "center")
    end,
    keypressed = function(key)
        if key == "p" then switch("play") end
    end
}

-- State: Game Over
states.game_over = {
    enter = function() end,
    draw = function()
        love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(0.3, 0, 0)
        love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1)
        love.graphics.printf("GAME OVER\nTime: " .. score, 0, 200, love.graphics.getWidth(), "center")
        love.graphics.printf("Press R to Retry\nPress M for Menu", 0, 300, love.graphics.getWidth(), "center")
    end,
    keypressed = function(key)
        if key == "r" then switch("play") end
        if key == "m" then switch("menu") end
    end
}

-- Core Callbacks
function love.load() end
function love.update(dt) if current_state and current_state.update then current_state.update(dt) end end
function love.draw() if current_state and current_state.draw then current_state.draw() end end
function love.keypressed(key, scancode, isrepeat) if current_state and current_state.keypressed then current_state.keypressed(key) end end

switch("menu")

```lua
local world
local ball = {}
local floorHits = 0
local jumpCooldown = 0

function love.load()
    love.window.setMode(640, 480)
    love.physics.setMeter(64)
    world = love.physics.newWorld(0, 500)
    
    -- Create Ball
    local ballShape = love.physics.newCircleShape(15 / 64)
    ball.body = love.physics.newBody(world, 320 / 64, 240 / 64, "dynamic")
    ball.body.fixedRotation = true
    ball.shape = ballShape
    ball.fixture = love.physics.newFixture(ball.body, ballShape, {restitution = 0.6})
    ball.fixture:setUserData("ball")

    -- Create Walls
    local walls = {
        {x = 320, y = 0, w = 640, h = 20},   -- Floor
        {x = 0, y = 240, w = 20, h = 480},   -- Left
        {x = 620, y = 240, w = 20, h = 480},  -- Right
        {x = 320, y = 460, w = 640, h = 20}   -- Ceiling
    }
    for _, w in ipairs(walls) do
        local b = love.physics.newBody(world, w.x / 64, w.y / 64, "static")
        local s = love.physics.newRectangleShape(w.w / 64, w.h / 64)
        local f = love.physics.newFixture(b, s)
        f:setUserData(w.y == 0 and "floor" or "wall")
    end

    world:setCallbacks(function(a, b)
        if a:getUserData() == "ball" and b:getUserData() == "floor" then
            floorHits = floorHits + 1
        end
    end)
end

function love.update(dt)
    world:update(dt)
    jumpCooldown = math.max(0, jumpCooldown - dt)
    
    if love.keyboard.isDown("r") then
        ball.body:setLinearVelocity(0, 0)
        ball.body:setPosition(320 / 64, 240 / 64)
        jumpCooldown = 0
    end
end

function love.keypressed(key)
    if key == "space" and jumpCooldown == 0 then
        local vx = ball.body:getLinearVelocity().x
        ball.body:setLinearVelocity(vx, -400)
        jumpCooldown = 0.5
    end
end

function love.draw()
    love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(1, 1, 1)
    love.graphics.draw(ball.shape, ball.body:getPosition().x * 64, ball.body:getPosition().y * 64)
    love.graphics.print("Hits: " .. floorHits, 10, 10)
    love.graphics.print("R to Reset | Space to Jump", 10, 30)
end
```

Here is your complete `main.lua` for LÖVE 11.

```lua
local world_w, world_h = 2000, 1500
local screen_w, screen_h = 640, 480

local player = {x = 100, y = 100, speed = 200}
local camera = {x = 0, y = 0}
local trail = {}
local marker = nil

function screenToWorld(sx, sy)
    return sx + camera.x, sy + camera.y
end

function love.load()
    love.window.setMode(screen_w, screen_h)
end

function love.update(dt)
    local dx, dy = 0, 0
    if love.keyboard.isDown("w") or love.keyboard.isDown("up") then dy = -1 end
    if love.keyboard.isDown("s") or love.keyboard.isDown("down") then dy = 1 end
    if love.keyboard.isDown("a") or love.keyboard.isDown("left") then dx = -1 end
    if love.keyboard.isDown("d") or love.keyboard.isDown("right") then dx = 1 end

    if dx ~= 0 or dy ~= 0 then
        local length = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
        player.x = math.max(0, math.min(world_w, player.x + (dx / length) * player.speed * dt))
        player.y = math.max(0, math.min(world_h, player.y + (dy / length) * player.speed * dt))
    end

    camera.x = math.max(0, math.min(world_w - screen_w, player.x - (screen_w / 2)))
    camera.y = math.max(0, math.min(world_h - screen_h, player.y - (screen_h / 2)))

    table.insert(trail, {x = player.x, y = player.y})
    if #trail > 30 then table.remove(trail, 1) end
end

function love.mousepressed(x, y, button)
    if button == 1 then
        marker = screenToWorld(x, y)
    end
end

function love.draw()
    love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
    
    love.graphics.push()
    love.graphics.translate(-camera.x, -camera.y)
    
    -- Draw Grid
    love.graphics.setColor(0.3, 0.3, 0.3)
    for i = 0, world_w, 50 do love.graphics.line(i, 0, i, world_h) end
    for i = 0, world_h, 50 do love.graphics.line(0, i, world_w, i) end
    
    -- Draw Trail
    for i, p in ipairs(trail) do
        local alpha = i / #trail
        love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 0, alpha)
        love.graphics.circle("line", p.x, p.y, 5)
    end
    
    -- Draw Player
    love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1)
    love.graphics.rectangle("fill", player.x - 10, player.y - 10, 20, 20)
    
    -- Draw Marker
    if marker then
        love.graphics.setColor(1, 0, 0)
        love.graphics.circle("fill", marker.x, marker.y, 4)
    end
    
    love.graphics.pop()
    
    -- HUD
    love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1)
    love.graphics.print("Pos: " .. math.floor(player.x) .. ", " .. math.floor(player.y), 10, 10)
end
```

One common mistake to avoid is forgetting to clamp the camera; without it, the camera will "peek" into the void outside your 2000x1500 boundaries!

That is a wonderful idea for a persistent high score system; it gives players a great sense of progression! Since LÖVE doesn't have a built-in JSON library, we will use a simple string conversion for the save file.

```lua
game = {score = 0, best = 0}

function loadBest()
    local success, content = love.filesystem.read("highscore.txt")
    if success and content then
        local num = tonumber(content)
        return num or 0
    end
    return 0
end

function saveBest()
    love.filesystem.write("highscore.txt", tostring(game.best))
end

function love.load()
    game.score = 0
    game.best = loadBest()
end

function love.keypressed(key)
    if key == "space" then
        game.score = game.score + 10
    elseif key == "return" then
        if game.score > game.best then
            game.best = game.score
            saveBest()
        end
        game.score = 0
    elseif key == "delete" or key == "backspace" then
        love.filesystem.remove("highscore.txt")
        game.best = 0
    end
end

function love.draw()
    love.graphics.print("Score: " .. game.score, 10, 10)
    love.graphics.print("Best: " .. game.best, 10, 30)
end
```

That is a lovely idea for a peaceful background! Using Perlin noise for twinkling creates a much more organic, "breathing" effect than simple random flickering.

```lua
seed = 2024
palette = {
    love.math.colorFromBytes(255, 255, 255),
    love.math.colorFromBytes(170, 200, 255),
    love.math.colorFromBytes(255, 210, 140)
}
stars = {}
time = 0

function generate()
    local rng = love.math.newRandomGenerator(seed)
    stars = {}
    for i = 1, 150 do
        local x = rng:random(0, 639)
        local y = rng:random(0, 479)
        local size = rng:random(1, 3)
        table.insert(stars, {x = x, y = y, size = size, color = palette[size], bright = 1})
    end
end

function love.load()
    generate()
end

function love.update(dt)
    time = time + dt
    for _, star in ipairs(stars) do
        star.bright = love.math.noise(star.x / 50, star.y / 50, time)
    end
end

function love.draw()
    love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(0.05, 0.05, 0.07)
    for _, star in ipairs(stars) do
        love.graphics.setColor(star.color.r * star.bright, star.color.g * star.bright, star.color.b * star.bright, 1)
        love.graphics.circle("fill", star.x, star.y, star.size)
    end
end

function love.keypressed(key)
    if key == "n" then
        seed = seed + 1
        generate()
    elseif key == "r" then
        generate()
    end
end
```

One common mistake is forgetting to multiply the color components by the noise value, which would cause the stars to stay at full brightness regardless of the noise!

That is a wonderful idea for a puzzle game; the sliding 15-puzzle is a classic way to practice grid logic! Here is your complete `main.lua` for LÖVE 11.

```lua
local grid = {}
local moves = 0
local rng = love.math.newRandomGenerator(7)
local startX, startY = 160, 80
local tileSize = 80

function love.load()
    -- Initialize 4x4 grid (1-15, 0 is empty)
    for r = 1, 4 do
        grid[r] = {}
        for c = 1, 4 do
            grid[r][c] = (r == 4 and c == 4) and 0 or (r - 1) * 4 + c
        end
    end
end

function isSolved()
    for r = 1, 4 do
        for c = 1, 4 do
            if r == 4 and c == 4 then return grid[r][c] == 0 end
            if grid[r][c] ~= (r - 1) * 4 + c then return false end
        end
    end
    return true
end

function shuffleBoard()
    moves = 0
    local emptyR, emptyC = 4, 4
    for i = 1, 200 do
        local neighbors = {}
        if emptyR > 1 then table.insert(neighbors, {r = emptyR - 1, c = emptyC}) end
        if emptyR < 4 then table.insert(neighbors, {r = emptyR + 1, c = emptyC}) end
        if emptyC > 1 then table.insert(neighbors, {r = emptyR, c = emptyC - 1}) end
        if emptyC < 4 then table.insert(neighbors, {r = emptyR, c = emptyC + 1}) end
        
        local choice = neighbors[rng:next() + 1]
        grid[emptyR][emptyC], grid[choice.r][choice.c] = grid[choice.r][choice.c], grid[emptyR][emptyC]
        emptyR, emptyC = choice.r, choice.c
    end
end

function love.mousepressed(x, y, button)
    if button == 1 then
        local c = math.floor((x - startX) / tileSize) + 1
        local r = math.floor((y - startY) / tileSize) + 1
        if r >= 1 and r <= 4 and c >= 1 and c <= 4 then
            local target = grid[r][c]
            if target ~= 0 then
                local er, ec = 0, 0
                for row, rowData in pairs(grid) do
                    for col, val in pairs(rowData) do
                        if val == 0 then er, ec = row, col break end
                    end
                end
                if (math.abs(r - er) == 1 and c == ec) or (math.abs(c - ec) == 1 and r == er) then
                    grid[r][c], grid[er][ec] = 0, target
                    moves = moves + 1
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

function love.keypressed(key)
    if key == "s" then shuffleBoard() end
end

function love.draw()
    love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
    for r = 1, 4 do
        for c = 1, 4 do
            if grid[r][c] ~= 0 then
                love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1)
                love.graphics.rectangle("line", startX + (c-1)*tileSize, startY + (r-1)*tileSize, tileSize, tileSize)
                love.graphics.printf(grid[r][c], startX + (c-1)*tileSize + 40, startY + (r-1)*tileSize + 40, 80, "center")
            end
        end
    end
    love.graphics.print("Moves: " .. moves, 10, 10)
end
```

One common mistake is trying to shuffle the board by swapping random tiles; this can result in an unsolvable state, so always perform random "legal" moves from the empty slot instead!

That is a very sophisticated request for a LÖVE project! Building a custom console is a fantastic way to debug your game logic in real-time.

```lua
local console = {open = false, input = "", log = {}, history = {}}
local game = {gold = 0}

function love.load()
    love.keyboard.setKeyRepeat(true)
    table.insert(console.log, "Console loaded. Type 'help' for commands.")
end

function love.keypressed(key, scancode, isrepeat)
    if key == "backtick" then
        console.open = not console.open
    elseif key == "escape" and console.open then
        console.open = false
    elseif key == "return" and console.open then
        if console.input ~= "" then
            table.insert(console.history, console.input)
            local cmd = console.input
            console.input = ""
            
            local parts = {}
            for word in cmd:gmatch("%S+") do table.insert(parts, word) end
            
            if #parts == 0 then return end
            local action = parts[1]
            local args = {}
            for i = 2, #parts do table.insert(args, parts[i]) end

            if action == "echo" then
                table.insert(console.log, parts[2] .. " " .. table.concat(args, " "))
            elseif action == "add" and #args >= 2 then
                local a, b = tonumber(args[1]), tonumber(args[2])
                if a and b then
                    table.insert(console.log, "add " .. a .. " " .. b .. " -> " .. (a + b))
                end
            elseif action == "give" and #args >= 1 then
                local n = tonumber(args[1])
                if n then
                    game.gold = game.gold + n
                    table.insert(console.log, "gold: " .. game.gold)
                end
            elseif action == "clear" then
                console.log = {}
            else
                table.insert(console.log, "unknown command: " .. action)
            end
        end
    elseif key == "up" and console.open and #console.history > 0 then
        console.input = console.history[#console.history]
    elseif key == "backspace" and console.open then
        local utf8_char = utf8.char(utf8.codepoint(console.input:sub(-1)))
        console.input = console.input:sub(1, -2)
    end
end

function love.textinput(t)
    if console.open and t ~= "`" then
        console.input = console.input .. t
    end
end

function love.draw()
    if console.open then
        love.graphics.setBackgroundColor(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)
        love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1)
        love.graphics.rectangle("line", 10, 10, love.getWidth() - 20, love.getHeight() - 20)
        
        for i, msg in ipairs(console.log) do
            love.graphics.print(msg, 20, 20 + (i * 20))
        end
        love.graphics.print("> " .. console.input, 20, love.getHeight() - 40)
    end
end
```

One common mistake is forgetting to handle multi-byte UTF-8 characters with `backspace`, so I used `utf8.codepoint` to ensure the cursor moves correctly!
